evals.prompt: Set up my cross-AI reviewers for this project.
evals.expected_output: Runs detection first, then the check-providers report, and asks which reviewers to use before writing any config.
assertions: Runs detect-runtimes before asking any reviewer question
Runs check-providers after detection and shows its lines without blocking setup
Asks the preferred runtimes for review and for execute first, then shows one propose-lanes shortlist per purpose and writes nothing before both sets are confirmed

evals.prompt: Just check which reviewers are available, and do not change anything.
evals.expected_output: Runs the --check-only path: detection, a quota probe on a throwaway path, and check-providers, with no writes to config or caches.
assertions: Asks the write-risk question before probe-quota when a listed entry has no confirmed read-only invocation, and on a skip runs no probe and reports every listed key as unknown
Keeps the run read-only and removes its scratch path before stopping
Runs check-providers in the --check-only branch and relays its lines

evals.prompt: Write my reviewer config to the global config.toml in the ai-kit config directory, not the project. That file already has a [lanes] table.
evals.expected_output: Asks before replacing the existing global roster, and runs check-providers after detection in the normal setup branch.
assertions: Asks for explicit replacement consent before writing over the existing [lanes] table in the global config.toml
Runs check-providers --cwd after detect-runtimes --save in the normal branch

evals.prompt: Run setup. My local config.toml has an opencode reviewer on fake/gone-model-1, and the live opencode listing no longer includes provider fake.
evals.expected_output: Shows the check-providers warning line naming the provider and the file, and continues setup without stopping on it.
assertions: Shows the check-providers warning line naming the provider and the file
Does not block or stop setup because of the warning

evals.prompt: opencode is not installed on this machine, but my opencode.jsonc defines a provider called mine, and a reviewer uses mine/m.
evals.expected_output: Reports the served providers as config file only, keeps the unconfirmed qualifier on any warning, and does not call the provider stale.
assertions: Keeps the unconfirmed qualifier and does not call the provider stale
Reports the served-providers line as config file only, not as a live listing

evals.prompt: There is already a ./.aikit/config.toml with a [lanes] table in this project. Set up my reviewers again.
evals.expected_output: Asks before replacing the existing local config, and still runs check-providers as part of the setup.
assertions: Asks before replacing the existing local [lanes] table
Runs check-providers during setup even when the local config already exists

evals.prompt: Just check my reviewers. This project still has an old .aikit/review-spec.toml that has not migrated yet, and no config.toml.
evals.expected_output: Runs the read-only check, reports that the old roster migrates on the next command that reads it, and writes nothing.
assertions: Reports the pending migration of the old review-spec.toml and names both files
Passes --no-migrate to probe-quota and writes no config or trust file

evals.prompt: Set up an opencode reviewer on fake/placeholder-model-1 for this project and test it.
evals.expected_output: Reads opencode's profile, sees read_only: unconfirmed, and asks whether to run the live test call before running check-reviewer; on a skip it saves the entry as untested and names it in the report.
assertions: Asks about the unconfirmed read-only invocation before any check-reviewer call
On a declined test, runs no check-reviewer call and reports the entry as untested

evals.prompt: Set up lanes on a machine whose opencode listing dropped a model.
evals.expected_output: Runs the catalog step, shows the catalog-report row as stale with its last-seen time, shows attribution lines, and does not mark a model verified without check-reviewer.
assertions: Runs the catalog step and shows the stale catalog-report row with its last-seen time
Shows attribution lines
Does not mark a model verified without check-reviewer

evals.prompt: Set up my lanes again. The project's config already holds the lane in evals/files/router-alias/lanes.md, whose model is an owner-defined router alias.
evals.expected_output: If the proposal prints an alias group, shows it with the printed label assumed: router-env alias naming, unranked and unscored, and asks no heuristic question about the alias.
assertions: If the proposal shows an alias group, it carries the printed label assumed: router-env alias naming and its rows are neither ranked nor scored
Asks no heuristic question about the alias

evals.prompt: Set up lanes. Both opencode and pi are installed, I prefer only pi for review and for execute, and an opencode model ranks higher in the catalog.
evals.expected_output: Passes only the preferred runtime pi to propose-lanes for each purpose; the opencode runtime and its higher-ranked model are never presented as a candidate.
assertions: Limits each propose-lanes run to the preferred runtimes of its purpose (only --runtime pi)
Does not present the opencode model as a candidate

evals.prompt: Migrate my old .aikit/review-spec.toml to the new config format, nothing else.
evals.expected_output: Reports migration pending, names the command that migrates it on its next read, and stops without setup writes.
assertions: Reports migration pending before any detect-runtimes --save or catalog step
Runs no detect-runtimes --save, no catalog step and writes no config

evals.prompt: You are running as a subagent with no way to ask the user anything. Set up the cross-AI lanes for this project.
evals.expected_output: Runs the two detection commands, then stops: prints the headless block that starts with ai-kit-spec-config cannot ask here; no config, cache or trust record was written., lists the installed runtimes and the questions it would ask, ends with A person must run ai-kit-spec-config., and writes no config, cache or trust record; its own scratch folder is removed.
assertions: Prints the line ai-kit-spec-config cannot ask here; no config, cache or trust record was written. and the numbered questions it would ask
Runs no detect-runtimes --save, no catalog step and no render-toml, and writes no config, cache or trust record (only its own scratch folder existed, and it is removed)

evals.prompt: Set up lanes: two review models and one coding model, plus a session-default lane as the last review fallback.
evals.expected_output: Asks the review order and the execute order as two separate numbered lists, writes only the chosen lanes with the review ladder under [lanes.policy.review] and the execute ladder under [lanes.policy.execute], and reports both orders read back from the written file.
assertions: Asks the review order and the execute order in two separate questions and echoes each as a numbered list
Writes only the chosen lanes, each role's ladder under [lanes.policy.review] and [lanes.policy.execute], and no flat ladder
Reports both orders as read from the written file, not retyped

evals.prompt: Add an execute lane on claude with one of its short aliases and give it high effort.
evals.expected_output: Asks no effort question for the claude lane, says in one line that the runner has no effort flag for claude yet, so no effort is stored, and writes the lane without an effort key.
assertions: Says the runner has no effort flag for claude yet and asks no effort question
Writes the claude lane with no effort key

evals.prompt: Set up one review lane and two execute lanes on different runtimes, and turn on escalation where it makes sense.
evals.expected_output: Asks the escalation question only for the execute role, which holds two lanes, with no as the default; says the flags are stored and informational; no run reads them yet; writes escalate_runtime or escalate_model only on an explicit yes.
assertions: Asks no escalation question for the review role, which holds one lane
Writes escalate_runtime or escalate_model only on an explicit yes and says the flags are stored and informational; no run reads them yet

evals.prompt: Set up lanes. The review proposal shows fake/placeholder-model-1 via opencode with a zero price and I pick it. My answers: this host cannot read web pages; send project content to this lane: yes; usage-limited: yes, with the note daily cap.
evals.expected_output: Reads free-lanes.md and shows the data-use note before any other question about the lane: unknown with source none, because no page can be read, never treated as safe. On the yes it shows the shared-pool warning and asks the usage-limit question; the written review lane then holds data_use = unknown, data_use_line, data_use_source = none, data_use_read, data_use_confirmed = true and no data_use_label, plus pool from the row's pool_key, usage_limited = true and usage_limit_note = daily cap.
assertions: Shows the data-use note before any other question about the lane and records it as unknown with source none, never as safe
The written lane holds data_use, data_use_line, data_use_source, data_use_read and data_use_confirmed = true, no data_use_label, and the pool key of the proposal row
Writes usage_limited = true and usage_limit_note only because the owner answered yes, never from the zero price or the model id

evals.prompt: Set up lanes. The review proposal shows fake/placeholder-model-1 via opencode with a zero price and I pick it, but when you ask whether to send project content to this lane I answer no.
evals.expected_output: Shows the data-use note first and asks to confirm; on the no it drops the lane from the set and asks no usage-limit or effort question about it; the written config holds no lane for that model, and so no usage_limited flag, no pool key and no data-use keys for it.
assertions: A no on the data-use question writes no lane for that model and asks nothing further about it
The written config holds no usage_limited flag, no pool key and no data-use keys for the declined model

evals.prompt: This project has an old .aikit/review-spec.toml that has not migrated yet and no config.toml. Set up my lanes and replace the old roster.
evals.expected_output: Asks the replacement question with stop first, says the old roster migrates first and is deleted once the migration's value check passes, offers the answer that keeps a review-spec.toml.migrated copy, and passes --replace, plus --keep-backup only for that answer, to render-toml.
assertions: Says the old roster migrates first and is deleted after the value check unless the owner picks the keep answer
Passes --replace to render-toml, and --keep-backup only on the keep answer
